en: He would deliver them from this ruin,
If the Creator was true,
Saying Kurasan would place it in their hands.
They would bind a rope around his waist,
These closed eyes would open,
The burning heart would be soothed,
Thus spoke Jeljetpes,
No soul surpassed him in wisdom,
When enraged, he equaled forty thousand men,
With courage equal to a thousand heroes,
Beginning with the hero,
Several of them in the night,
Two went with him to the people in a boat,
They disembarked beside the right-hand mound,
He made every soul submit,
If you looked, his station was lofty,
He narrowed one of his eyes,
What he said was never mistaken,
He knew the Chinese secrets well,
When enraged, his piercing eyes stayed open,
Eloquent in speech and rich in words,
Such a man was truthful in speech,
He came forth among mankind,
He awoke and sat up,
His dark eyes opened,
A sage upheld by heaven and earth.
God became the cause of my benefit,
Calling the hand of the witness a poet,
We were a people with the bellies of thousands,
Asking him to tell one piece of news,
The sun shone upon the living,
Asking him to name one neighbor,
Taking punishment upon himself,
Amid the work of dawn and grief,
Pleading with the Creator,
Like a river against the hollow of the hand,
Toward the truth that raised the blue sky,
Thundering at the hour of dawn,
Saying God would grant it amid torment,
The happiness of this poor man,
If the Creator is true,
Saying our gathered host would deliver him,
The heart is calmed from the cradle,
These eyes are opened through labor,
The heart that burned like fire is calmed,
So died my Zhelzhetpes,
The soul between those who took the shot,
The hero fixed his eyes upon the fortress,
The hero knew and understood the ambush,
His heroism was of another kind,
This shelter still had distance to cover,
Now for the elder people who remained,
A glowing ember seen in the night,
Bound to the warrior soul,
If you look, it fulfilled the hero's aim,
My curse became a champion,
What he said came in ordered lines,
His Chinese speech was clear,
His frost-bound eyes were clearly unwetted,
Eloquent of tongue and rich in words,
No living soul here could restrain his teeth,
Like joy mingled with torment,
He drove them onward through thought,
His eyes looked on as he spoke,
His hand pleaded from the heart.
From calamity beyond the reach of sight,
Born truly resilient even when exhausted,
He had words spoken by destiny,
When he won a name, he had honor,
He had the splendor of steel in combat,
A heroic man, a warrior’s lamp,
He had words worthy of a lion,
The sacred Jeljetpes,
Spoke of the peril befalling the guileless hero,
Wearing a mottled blue cloak,
His wings awakened across many lands,
The excessive hardship and torment,
He foresaw it without being told,
He would not surrender to a knowing warrior,
He would not plead with a true fool,
Ah, if there came a dark night,
If the world with children saw daylight,
He watched the path toward the summer pasture,
Even when his clear hope broke, he did not plead,
His wisdom was a myriad rivers,
Ah, Jeljetpes appeared,
A life that had seen its fill,
The children set it in the proper place,
The tall red camel of the summer pasture,
His gray leather pouch with its moon-shaped ornament,
Was hung around his neck,
He mounted the ancestor’s camel,
Appealing to the ancestor’s spirit,
To elder Kozbul, the forefather,
Then drawing close beside him,
Keeping watch across Talas,
Supporting his blinded companion,
Loading the giant’s burden,
He tended the honored one,
Leading the noble camel by its halter,
Taking the giant and caring for him,
Their eyes looked fondly on the children,
Oysul-Ata’s red camel.
A soul like you truly carried it there,
Spreading his hands and saying amen,
Pursuing the claim from its beginning,
He took form again in life,
I have a lamb already promised,
O living creature, asking that you give it,
He lay uselessly upon the glowing mound,
Separated from the place of a father,
Guarded in the place of a mother,
A pure wish spoken at the grave,
He pondered the plea of his tongue,
All of it comes from me, sovereign,
The crown of the divided rope,
A wondrous people fell to the warrior,
Opening his palms and reciting a prayer,
May my poor people consign him to earth,
Zhelzhetpes, gray-maned Zhelzhetpes,
He looked into his eyes and struck,
From a people sweeter than honey,
Forty yearning souls remained,
Now he sent the soul into holy war,
Do not let all of you ramble,
It was the pouring out of earthly wealth,
When he gathered those in torment,
Opening his hands and saying amen,
When only a bow-like value remained,
From the plain near good fortune,
It came from the glowing hill,
He mounted a moon-white horse,
The sorrowful one wore another coat,
He settled the place of punishment,
They bound him and left him alone,
He wore a blue patterned coat,
He mounted the gray horse named Koktemir,
The racehorse the hero mounted,
He swiftly tied its straight tail,
He stood resolutely before his people,
The Kyrgyz burned and became fire.
His armor was steel, his poison fierce.
It was the hour he cut down whoever met him.
His nose rose like a rugged peak.
His eyes and coat were hard as iron.
Alas, submitting to God’s command,
He drove a people numbering sevenfold.
The beautiful maiden stood apart.
His terror was singular and his venom fierce.
O God, set me straight.
In the measure of the present age,
Saying, “I am gone,” he abandoned hope of life.
As though a savage dog had sunk its teeth in,
Between his two shoulder blades,
Idle boys cast knucklebones.
Many came near him.
The grassy meadow held grazing livestock.
Wrapped in calamity,
He lay as a pale wrestler might lie.
Black brows stood over his eyes.
Even a horse herder had never seen his like.
Beside him lay a rope of measured length.
He was a servant of Almighty God.
The Creator makes every kind.
On the earth he rode a brocade-clad horse.
His nape was like a stallion’s, his coat mysterious.
Then another man emerged.
Two wealthy souls appeared.
With two breaths they cried, “The enemy!”
He became chief among the heroes.
A creature that lapped blood from the earth,
A companion who rode upon the ground,
Or perhaps it was Badirek.
The dominion of earth and water,
Was he one whom the earth itself touched?
Kaisan kept him captive.
His eye was of black stone.
Let us leave aside whoever encountered him.
This was hardship itself,
They set out after riding at a trot,
Crossing the bloody marsh by night,
Calling it the dark eye of hardship,
There it lay fitted among the rocks,
A suffering people among the Kyrgyz nation,
Even the eyes that looked back,
Finding no mountain farther within,
Finding no enemy to fight,
One of them grew weary,
A fool who fled from labor,
Suited to what no eye could face,
Against the wrathful bloodshed,
Bound and given over as befitted them,
The poor twins fell into hardship,
The multitude drove them onward.
Their eyes read the signs of torment,
For snow there was only God,
They fought their way back through many lands,
There was no accustomed refuge in those lands,
It suited what they called Osh,
Believing him dead, his spirit sank,
The false world held countless men without arrows,
Lofty even amid evil,
The poor remnants who had strayed,
When the formidable host surrounded them,
Their extraordinary spirits sank,
Their soaked souls cried out,
The ravenous taker of souls,
As though reaching a hand into their shelter,
As though about to tear out their souls,
While they stood trembling in fear,
Blood drained away beneath God’s gaze,
Strength left the heroes,
Fearing disaster if they moved,
Hardship dimmed their failing eyes.
One ladle remained from all that was left,
Calling the humiliation within it humiliation,
Saying he should be freed from disgrace,
Those whose hearts could no longer endure,
What could not be was imposed again,
They descended from life in the place of honor,
Their faces turned pale,
As he stood speaking loudly like this,
Was it present within his grave?
He turned the seat of hell,
A fortress against four stratagems,
He cast light upon the company of nine,
He shared with those who had not divided,
He himself was among the divided,
O, toward the accursed one,
This was no mere word of Kenen,
Joining what had been severed,
Gathering what had been scattered,
Raising the dead back beside the living,
Making the blessing known,
Nurturing the poor,
Protecting the helpless,
That father burdened with grief,
His dark eyes watched in pursuit,
Sharing with those who had not divided,
It appeared that the children would remain,
To the sorrowful one who had arrived,
It was the moment to find a way,
A means remained amid the hardship,
His was a soul that stood ready to save,
The people bristled and waited,
A coat was drawn over his shoulders,
Calling him enemy, they cast him from life,
The wailing, destitute people,
A people fleeing from the wrathful one,
A people driven from their beloved souls,
Abandoning Talas and trampling onward.
Hardened beneath the world and sun,
The old man grazed his herd among the rocks,
Having both forbidden and lawful beasts slaughtered,
For the soul offered by the rich man,
Bringing his true weapon to bear,
